name: Dreamoon and Sums
description: Dreamoon loves summing up something for no reason. One day he obtains two integers a and b occasionally. He wants to calculate the sum of all nice integers. The answer may be large, so please print its remainder modulo 1 000 000 007 ( 10 9 + 7 ). Can you compute it faster than Dreamoon?
input_specification: The single line of the input contains two integers a , b ( 1 ≤ a , b ≤ 10 7 ).
output_specification: Print a single integer representing the answer modulo 1 000 000 007 ( 10 9 + 7 ).
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 476C — Dreamoon and Sums [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
